_doc: THE ENSEMBLE — the Switch~ piece's parts as notation data (container 6, 6.0, 2026-10-23 — RUNNING_LOG §24; the shape and every mechanism are pieces 4 · 5 · 6's). Indexed by the composer score's LAYER, which is the IR's "part". Read by layout.js (clef, written pitch, staves), coords.js (the frame), the extractor (the check below).
_check: tools/notate_section.js refuses to extract when a part's `id` or `short` differs from the score's tracks[part] — the registry cannot drift from the composer score silently. The ids and shorts below are composer.html's TRACKS exactly; tools/palette_check.js guards the other direction.
_layersNote: composer.html: META_LAYER = 8 (= tracks.length), CURVE_LAYERS = [9, 10, 11] (the curve windows A / B / C, over Piano · Violin · Cello). Neither is a part.
_transposeConvention: WRITTEN = SOUNDING + transpose semitones (layout.js line 75, and applied at line 965 — read in the code, not taken from a comment, during the port). The IR is always SOUNDING pitch (#5's D9); the shift happens at layout only, and the note is spelled from the written pitch. Piece #5's bass clarinet (+14, written a major ninth above sounding) is the precedent that fixes the sign.
_pitchForm: A TRANSPOSED score — his "a" (2026-10-23, RUNNING_LOG §24): the clarinet in B♭ (+2), the alto sax in E♭ (+9). "In C" = `transpose` removed from parts 1 and 2.

parts._clefNote: Flute in C, treble, non-transposing. The piccolo / alto flute doublings are not taken (D1).

parts._transposeNote: B♭ clarinet: written a major second (2 semitones) ABOVE sounding — the SI2 manual: "Instrument part to be written a major second higher". The IR keeps SOUNDING pitch (piece 4's D9); the shift is applied at layout. In C = this field removed.
E♭ alto saxophone: written a major sixth (9 semitones) ABOVE sounding — the SI2 manual: "Instrument part to be written a major sixth higher". In C = this field removed.

lines.instrument: shime daiko (or a snare drum — PERFORMANCE_NOTES #5)

parts._staffNote: THE UNPITCHED STAFF — his "b" (2026-10-23, RUNNING_LOG §24: "can this be reversed later when it comes time to notate?" — yes: this entry is the whole of it; Decibel's hidden one-line form is one edit). PROVISIONAL: piece 6's eight-line staff of 2026-10-04 (its 755ed29, after Ferneyhough's Bone Alphabet — one line per instrument, 2 ss apart, no clef, the short names in the gutter, a note ON the line of its instrument by its technique key's prefix), for the SAME eight Abbey Road instruments this rack carries (bank/perc_selection.json). His instruments from the call's list (D10) replace the lines when chosen; the order is then his. | piece 6: THE UNPITCHED STAFF, piece #6's type (after Ferneyhough's Bone Alphabet — one line per instrument, 2 ss apart, no clef, the short names in the gutter, a note ON the line of its instrument by its technique key's prefix): EIGHT lines here, for his TENTATIVE list of 2026-10-04 (COMPOSITION_NOTES DEC-6). THE ORDER IS PROVISIONAL AND THE AI'S — his rule of piece #6 applied as far as eight instruments allow ("high to low, no two neighbours of one material"): metal · skin · metal · skin · metal · skin · wood · skin. A staff type's design is HIS (the protocol's 6.2): put to him; reordering is this list.

parts._clefNote: THE PITCHED PERCUSSION — every pitched instrument he owns on this ONE five-line staff (D10: the vibraphone, the glockenspiel, the crotales, the xylophone, the marimba). Treble clef, NO transposition in the registry: the Ricotti library maps every one of the four at its WRITTEN pitch (crotales C4–C6 · glockenspiel G3–C6 · xylophone F3–B6 · marimba C2–C7 as keyed), so the key the score sends IS the note to write — the crotales and the glockenspiel SOUND two octaves higher, the xylophone one, the marimba as written. Which instrument a note is for, and two at once ("opposite beaming or something like that"), is a DEVICE SHEET when the music reaches it (6.7). The marimba below middle C wants a bass clef; he is unlikely to use it. The part id is still "vibraphone" and the recipe key "bowed_vibraphone" — piece #6's, kept (docs/NAMING.md § 1).
parts._shortNote: His word (2026-10-23): "perc for both no vib" — the pitched lane is named Perc in the gutter like the unpitched one: one player, two staves, a brace. The id `vibraphone` and the recipe key `bowed_vibraphone` stay (NAMING § 1).

parts._stavesNote: ONE lane, taller (composer 2026-09-11, RUNNING_LOG §382): a grand staff inside the one-lane-per-part model. weight 1.576 (§401k, was 2): the two staves sit 6 ss apart (container grandStaff.interStaffGapSs), centred in the lane, and the lane holds exactly the air a single player's lane has above and below its staff — lane = unit + 4 + 6 ss, so w = 1 + 10/u with u = 131.6/(6 + w) → u 17.37 ss, w 1.576. The other six lanes grow from 16.46 to 17.37 ss (+5.5 %). A note at or above splitMidi (middle C) goes on the upper staff, below it on the lower — the plain rule; a per-note override is later work.

parts._clefNote: Bass clef, as pieces #5 and #6. A tenor clef for a high stretch: 6.10, not built.

_groupsNote: Score order top to bottom: the three winds in a bracket · the ONE percussionist's two parts (the unpitched staff, the pitched staff) in a BRACE, joined into one lane of the frame, 6 ss apart (piece 6's 755ed29) · the piano's grand staff (piece 4) · the two strings in a bracket. NO STAFF FOR THE ELECTRONICS (piece 6's D8). THE WEIGHTS (the percussion 1.888, the piano 1.576) are the earlier pieces' arithmetic for their own lane counts — provisional until the page is looked at.
